name: The Gates Scholarship
value: Funding for the full cost of attendance not already covered by other financial aid (as determined by the FAFSA or the college's methodology)
deadline: Class of 2027 application opened July 15, 2026 and closed September 15, 2026; semifinalist phase December 2026 to January 2027, finalist interviews March 2027, selection April 2027.
apply: Create a profile and apply online at thegatesscholarship.org; semifinalists complete further materials and finalists interview.
eligibility: High school seniors who are Pell-eligible, US citizens or permanent residents, with a minimum cumulative weighted GPA of 3.3 on a 4.0 scale, planning to enroll full time in a four-year degree at a US accredited not-for-profit college or university.
notes: The Class of 2027 deadline (September 15, 2026) has passed. Ideal candidates are in the top 10% of their class with demonstrated leadership and personal success skills.

name: Dell Scholars Program
value: $20,000 flexible scholarship plus a laptop, book credits and emergency funds; can also be used for graduate school, loan repayment, study abroad and internship stipends
deadline: Application opens October 1, 2026; deadline January 12, 2027; finalists announced January 21, 2027.
apply: Submit the online application; finalists then provide a high school transcript, FAFSA Submission Summary and an online recommendation for an independent selection committee.
eligibility: High school seniors graduating from a Texas high school who participated in an approved college readiness program in grades 11 and 12, are Pell Grant eligible, have at least a 2.4 GPA, and plan to enroll at an accredited four-year public college or university in Texas.
notes: The current official eligibility list is Texas-only (Texas high school and Texas public four-year college). Participation in an approved college readiness program is required.

name: Chick-fil-A Community Scholars
value: Up to $25,000 (one-time award, may be disbursed over 1 to 6 years); 13 awards per year, plus a year-long leadership development and mentorship program
deadline: November 3, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Central Time (online recommendations due three business days after the deadline).
apply: Apply online through Scholarship America with a current transcript, the first two pages of parents' IRS 1040 (or Canadian T-1) and at least one online recommendation.
eligibility: High school seniors (also undergraduate and graduate students) with a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA on a 4.0 scale, involved in community service, extracurriculars and/or leadership in the 12 months before the deadline, who will be 18 by July 15, 2027 and live in the US, Puerto Rico or Canada. DACA and international students are eligible.
notes: Selection weighs academics, activities, community service, recommendations, financial need and fit with Chick-fil-A's core values. Chick-fil-A employees and dependents or spouses of employees or Operators are not eligible.

name: Toyota Scholarship Program (Making Life Easier Scholars)
value: Up to $30,000 over four years ($7,500 per year); up to 50 awards per year
deadline: 2027-28 application dates not posted; the official page says the program is currently closed, cycle details are tentative, and all applicants will be notified by the end of February 2027.
apply: Apply online through Scholarship America with a Partner Verification Form signed by a Toyota nonprofit partner, an official transcript and a 2025 IRS Form 1040, plus essay responses.
eligibility: High school seniors, graduates or undergraduates who are members or recent alumni (within 3 years) of a designated Toyota nonprofit partner (Junior Achievement chapters, Boys & Girls Clubs, specific high schools and others) in AL, AZ, CA, GA, IN, KY, MI, MS, MO, NV, NC, PR, TN, TX or DC, with a minimum 2.0 GPA and planning full-time enrollment in 2027-28.
notes: Selection is based on financial need, community involvement and essay responses. Check the 2027 partner list PDF to see whether your organization or high school qualifies.

name: McDonald's HACER National Scholarship
value: $1 million in scholarships awarded to up to 100 students nationwide
deadline: 2027 application dates not yet posted; the official page says the application period is now closed.
apply: Online application with transcript, personal statement, online letter of recommendation and list of community service; semifinalists complete the FAFSA; selection includes a personal interview (in person or by phone).
eligibility: High school seniors under 21 with a minimum 2.8 GPA who are legal US residents, US citizens or DREAMER/DACA recipients, eligible to attend a two- or four-year college, university or vocational/technical school full time in the academic year after selection.
notes: Selection weighs academic achievement, financial need, community involvement, the personal statement and an interview. The eligibility page read does not state a heritage requirement; confirm current rules when the cycle opens.

name: Jimmy Rane Foundation Scholarship
value: $500 to $6,000 per year, renewable annually for up to four academic years (eight semesters)
deadline: Application opens December 1, 2026 and closes February 5, 2027; recommendation letters due February 10, 2027. Awardees notified by phone in mid-April.
apply: Apply through the foundation's online portal with SAT/ACT scores, financial information and recommendation letters.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors (spring/summer 2027) with a minimum 3.0 GPA who are permanent residents of AL, AR, DE, FL, GA, IL, IN, IA, KS, KY, LA, MD, MS, MO, NE, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OK, PA, SC, TN, TX, VA, WV or DC and US citizens or permanent residents. College freshmen and sophomores (2.75 GPA, age 20 or under on August 1, 2027) may also apply.
notes: Financial need is an important factor, along with goals, academic preparation, self-motivation, leadership and community involvement. Not for intercollegiate athletes (prior semester) or online-only degree programs; households of Great Southern Wood Preserving employees are ineligible.

name: Sachs Foundation Undergraduate Scholarship
value: $10,000 to $12,500 per year, renewable for up to four years ($40,000 to $50,000 total)
deadline: Applications are available each year January 1 to March 15 (recommendation letters by March 31); finalists notified in late April and attend a June finalist program in Colorado Springs.
apply: Apply online with transcript, two non-relative recommendations, two 500-word personal statements, FAFSA Student Aid Report and household tax return information; optional portfolio.
eligibility: Black high school seniors who have been full-time Colorado residents for at least three years.
notes: The page gives the recurring January 1 to March 15 window without a year. FAFSA and tax information are required; late or incomplete applications are not considered.

name: Horatio Alger Scholarships for High School Seniors (Denny Sanford, Washington Foundation and Bergeron awards)
value: Denny Sanford awards: Arizona State 25 x $10,000; Augustana 6 x $25,000; Black Hills State 12 x $12,500; Dakota State 15 x $10,000; Long Island University 6 x $40,000. Dennis & Phyllis Washington Foundation (Montana): 50 x $10,000 plus $5,000 institutional match. Bergeron Everglades Environmental Steward (Florida): 4 x $20,000.
deadline: Senior applicants apply December 1 to February 15 (noon ET); year not stated on the overview page.
apply: One online application covers all eligible awards: essays on adversity and the American Dream, counselor certification, an adult support form, transcripts and income verification.
eligibility: US citizens enrolled full time as high school seniors with adjusted gross family income of $100,000 or less, who show integrity and perseverance in overcoming adversity and take part in co-curricular and community service activities; minimum GPA 2.0 (state awards) or 2.5 (Denny Sanford awards); must start a bachelor's degree right after high school.
notes: The $25,000 Horatio Alger National Scholarship is for high school juniors; seniors may apply only for these college-specific and state awards. Denny Sanford awards require attending the named university; Washington awards require Montana residence and specified Montana campuses; Bergeron requires Florida residence and environmental studies.

name: Royal Neighbors of America Member Scholarships
value: Award amounts not stated on the official scholarship page
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; the 2026 application ran January 5 to March 2, 2026 (midnight Central Time).
apply: Get your Royal Neighbors certificate number, create an online account, complete the application and upload transcripts.
eligibility: Beneficial members of Royal Neighbors of America (insured under a Royal Neighbors life insurance certificate, or an annuity or settlement contract owner) over age 16, with a high school transcript showing at least a 2.5 GPA, pursuing a trade, associate, bachelor's or graduate degree at an accredited institution.
notes: Requires membership in the fraternal life insurer. Winners are chosen at Royal Neighbors' discretion with a judging panel; some related parties (such as dependents of board members and senior executives) are ineligible.

name: Work Ethic Scholarship Program
value: Awards range from $500 to $34,000 (average about $9,100)
deadline: Four rounds a year; the 2026 deadlines are April 30, June 30, August 30 and October 31, with decisions about two months after each deadline.
apply: Sign the S.W.E.A.T. Pledge, record a short video introduction, provide two references, and upload transcripts and tuition documentation at mikeroweworks.applyists.net.
eligibility: US citizens who are high school seniors or graduates enrolling in an approved skilled-trades program of two years or less at an accredited school.
notes: For trade and technical training only, not four-year degrees. Selection centers on work ethic, and the video carries heavy weight. An official tuition bill or cost statement is required.

name: TheDream.US National Scholarship
value: Up to $33,000 in tuition and fees for a bachelor's degree plus up to $6,000 for books, supplies and transportation
deadline: The official page says the next application round opens November 1, 2026; the prior round ran November 1, 2025 to February 28, 2026.
apply: Follow the step-by-step Application Guide and apply online during the open round.
eligibility: First-generation immigrant students who are undocumented (with or without DACA or TPS), arrived in the US before age 16, have a minimum 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale, show significant unmet financial need (not Pell eligible), qualify for in-state tuition at a partner college and enroll full time in an associate or bachelor's program.
notes: Usable only at about 80 partner colleges (Texas institutions, online programs and most private colleges excluded). Arrival and graduation cutoff dates are set per cycle; confirm them when the next round opens.

provider: Asian & Pacific Islander American Scholarship Fund (APIA Scholars)
name: APIA Scholarship
value: $2,500 one-year awards to $20,000 multi-year awards
deadline: 2027-28 cycle opens November 15, 2026 and closes January 15, 2027 at 5 p.m. ET; notifications April 15, 2027.
apply: Complete the online application; see the FAQ and Application Guide on the APIA Scholars site.
eligibility: US citizens, nationals or permanent residents (citizens of the Marshall Islands, Federated States of Micronesia and Palau also eligible) enrolling or continuing as degree-seeking undergraduates at a US accredited college, without a prior bachelor's degree. Students from all backgrounds may apply.
notes: Selection prioritizes significant financial need, first-generation students and those at or below the poverty line. Funded by corporate and foundation partners including FedEx, Nike, McDonald's, Disney, Toyota and the Walmart Foundation. The eligibility text still cites fall 2026 enrollment; confirm when the application opens.

name: Earl Woods Scholar Program
value: Renewable annual scholarship for up to four years plus mentorship, internship and summer enrichment help, career development and workshops (dollar amount not stated)
deadline: 2027 application dates not posted on the official page.
apply: Students from invited areas or high schools apply through the TGR Foundation online application.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors from a geographic area and/or high school invited to apply, with a minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale, demonstrated financial need and commitment to community service, enrolling full time at a US accredited not-for-profit university.
notes: Invitation-only by area or school (TGR Learning Labs are in Anaheim, Atlanta, Augusta, Los Angeles and Philadelphia). Scholars must attend a summer Pre-College Retreat and Scholarship Orientation.

name: ANS Incoming Freshman Scholarship
value: $1,000 each; up to ten awarded annually
deadline: Applications open November 1; incoming freshman scholarship deadline is April 1 (annual)
apply: Apply through the ANS scholarship application with a 500-word essay on intended study, proof of enrollment at a 4-year institution, list of activities and honor societies, and two STEM teacher/counselor/employer recommendations.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors enrolling full-time at a 4-year college in a STEM program with an interest in nuclear science and technology; high school academic achievement above 3.5 or equivalent.
notes: Recipients must become ANS student members once undergraduate studies begin to receive funds. AP courses and test scores recommended. Citizenship not stated for this award.

name: STEM Stars Actuarial Scholars Program
value: $20,000 total ($5,000 per year for up to four years), plus mentorship, internships, job shadowing and exam resources
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; applications reopen in the fall. The 2026 deadline was February 27, 2026.
apply: Apply online through the Foundation's Submittable portal when the cycle reopens.
eligibility: High school seniors who are mathematically talented and interested in the actuarial profession.
notes: Distinct from the Foundation's Modeling the Future Challenge. Other Actuarial Foundation scholarships are for current undergraduates.

name: CME Group Beef Industry Scholarship
value: Ten scholarships of $1,500 each
deadline: Application for 2027 now open; deadline not stated on the scholarship page. The prior cycle deadline was November 7, 2025 (5 pm Central).
apply: Apply online through the ReviewR portal linked from the scholarship page: one-page letter of intent on beef-industry career goals, essay of 750 words or less on an industry issue, and two letters of recommendation.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors or full-time undergraduates enrolling at a two- or four-year institution for 2027-2028 who show commitment to a beef-industry career (education, communications, production, research or related). Applicant or family must be a National Cattlemen's Beef Association member.
notes: Deadline typically falls in early November, so check the page soon.

name: ScholarSHPE for Graduating High School Seniors
value: Amounts vary by award (SHPE reports more than 1,500 scholarships totaling over $6,000,000 since 2018)
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; the 2026 application window was February 2 to February 16, 2026.
apply: Apply online through SHPE's ScholarSHPE application during the winter window.
eligibility: Active SHPE members who are high school seniors with a minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA, a declared STEM major, and plans to enroll at an accredited two- or four-year college.
notes: Citizenship not required for SHPE-funded awards; some corporate-sponsored awards may require it. Short application window.

name: NSBE Jr. High School Senior Scholarships (Graduating Senior, Leroy Callendar, Golden Torch)
value: NSBE Jr. Graduating Senior $500; Leroy Callendar NSBE Jr. $500; NSBE Jr. Golden Torch $1,000
deadline: Fall 2026 Scholarship Cycle will open soon; deadlines not yet posted. GPA verification window runs September 1 to February 26, 2027.
apply: Apply through NSBE's scholarship portal (SurveyMonkey Apply) when the Fall 2026 cycle opens.
eligibility: High school seniors (12th grade) who are registered, paid NSBE members pursuing engineering, computer science, mathematics or a related STEM field; minimum GPA 3.0 (Golden Torch 3.5). U.S. citizens, permanent residents and non-U.S. citizens may apply.
notes: The Fall 2025 portal listed the Graduating Senior award at $1,000; current nsbe.org listing shows $500.

name: EAA Post-Secondary Scholarships
value: Varies by scholarship; the most recent cycle awarded over $237,000 to 39 students
deadline: Applications open October 1 to December 19 of each year; the next application opens October 1, 2026
apply: Apply online during the October 1 to December 19 window; late applications not accepted.
eligibility: Current and incoming post-secondary students (including graduating high school seniors), at least 16, with a minimum 2.5 unweighted GPA, pursuing pilot training, aeronautical engineering, aviation management, A&P maintenance or related study at a college, university, technical school or community college. U.S. or Canadian citizens/residents or students with a valid study visa.
notes: EAA members and active chapter members are prioritized. Funds must be used by March 1 following the award year. Individual scholarships may require a higher GPA.

name: AEA Educational Foundation Scholarships
value: About 16 named awards from $1,000 to $5,000 (e.g., Aircraft Lighting International $5,000, James Hammond Joubert Memorial $5,000, Gogo $2,500, Lee Tarbox Memorial $2,500)
deadline: 2027-28 application not yet open; AEA says to check back in October. The 2026-27 deadline has passed.
apply: Submit the AEA Educational Foundation online scholarship application when it reopens in October.
eligibility: High school seniors or college students planning to attend or attending a program in avionics or aircraft maintenance (some awards: aviation management or Aviation Technician Certification).
notes: One application covers the various named awards.

provider: NAWIC Founders' Scholarship Foundation (National Association of Women in Construction)
name: NFSF Construction Trades Scholarship
value: Awards start at $2,000 (NFSF awards over $600,000 per year across its programs)
deadline: Applications accepted September through March 6 of the next year for the following academic year; exact 2027 date not separately posted
apply: Apply through nfsf.nawic.org (or email materials to nfsf@nawic.org): application, course description and cost, one-page financial need statement, activities list, employment history and essay responses.
eligibility: Students enrolled or enrolling in an approved construction-related craft or trade training program (apprenticeship, community college or technical school) in the United States. High school seniors are eligible for the trades scholarship only.
notes: High school seniors are not eligible for NFSF's undergraduate degree scholarship. Application materials include a financial need statement. An older NFSF form listed a February 28 deadline; confirm on nfsf.nawic.org.

name: NAHJ Scholarships
value: $2,000 to $6,000 by award (e.g., White House Correspondents' Association $6,000; Lori Montenegro, Cecilia Alvear, Dunia Elvir $5,000; Maria Elena Salinas $2,500; Ruben Salazar $2,000)
deadline: Next cycle dates not yet posted; the last posted deadline was December 28, 2025.
apply: Apply via the NAHJ online portal with resume, two recommendation letters, transcript, essay (500 words max) and up to three work samples.
eligibility: College-bound high school seniors, undergraduates and graduate students with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or better attending four-year or community colleges in the U.S. or Puerto Rico, pursuing journalism.
notes: Deadline has fallen in late December, so watch for the new cycle in the fall.

provider: Florida Engineering Society / Florida Engineering Foundation
name: FES High School Senior Engineering Scholarships
value: $36,000 in engineering scholarships funded for the 2026-2027 school year (individual amounts per application)
deadline: February 15, 2027 (application posts December 2026)
apply: Submit the FES High School Scholarship Submittal Form with the Excel application, certified transcripts, signed applicant and counselor certifications, and official AP/IB/AICE results.
eligibility: Florida high school seniors with a minimum 3.5 GPA (4.0 scale) and minimum SAT/ACT scores (per application), U.S. citizens or permanent residents, who will enroll in an ABET-accredited engineering program.
notes: Test score minimums are specified in the application rather than on the page.

name: MSPE High School Senior Scholarships
value: Named memorial awards (Kenneth B. Fishbeck, Harry R. Ball, B. Lang) plus university-specific awards at 9 Michigan institutions; amounts not stated
deadline: 2027 application to be announced later in the year; the 2026 application is closed.
apply: Submit the online application with transcript, SAT score, 250-word essay on engineering motivation, senior course list, and free MSPE/NSPE student membership application.
eligibility: Michigan resident high school seniors and U.S. citizens with a minimum 3.0 GPA (10th to 11th grade) accepted into an engineering program at an ABET-accredited Michigan institution. Computer science excluded.

name: NJCPA High School Scholarship
value: $1,500 for one year, plus an NJCPA mentor through college
deadline: December 7, 2026 (11:59 p.m.); finalists notified by January 4, 2027; virtual interviews January 16, 2027
apply: Complete the online application with a 450 to 500 word essay on what inspired you to choose accounting, transcript and test scores, and a guidance counselor form; finalists interview virtually.
eligibility: New Jersey resident, college-bound high school seniors (public, private/parochial or homeschool) planning to major in accounting or earn at least 24 accounting credits; U.S. citizen or permanent resident; must meet one of: 3-year GPA 3.2+, SAT 1260+, or ACT 26+.
notes: The 3.2 GPA is one of three alternative academic benchmarks. Interview date has no makeup.

provider: Washington CPA Foundation (Washington Society of CPAs)
name: Associate Accounting Scholarship
deadline: Application opens October 13, 2026; due April 13, 2027
apply: Apply online with evidence of community involvement, transcripts, three essays (500 words max each) and one reference contact.
eligibility: High school seniors entering any Washington state college or university (or students at a Washington community college) who plan to major in accounting or pursue a CPA credential; minimum 2.5 high school GPA.
notes: The page's eligibility line still says fall 2026 while the dates are for the 2026-27 cycle; confirm the entry term with the Foundation.

name: MOCPA High School Senior Accounting Scholarship
value: $500 toward accounting education
deadline: Details and application links for the 2026-2027 program to be posted in the fall; deadline not yet posted.
apply: Apply through the MOCPA scholarships page once the application posts.
eligibility: Free MOCPA high school student members who are Missouri residents and U.S. citizens (or children of MOCPA members), enrolling at a Missouri community college or university upon graduation and declared accounting majors.
notes: Winners selected on personal and academic experiences and potential to become a CPA. Student membership is free.

name: AMT Student Scholarships
value: Amount not stated on the official page
deadline: Applications accepted starting Oct. 1, 2026; must be submitted by April 1, 2027
apply: Complete the online application with two letters of reference, a 500-word essay on career choice, and proof of enrollment or admission into a fall program.
eligibility: High school seniors or graduates (GED accepted), or current AMT members, enrolling in a regionally accredited college or university in a course of study leading to an AMT-certified field (e.g., medical technology, medical assisting, phlebotomy, dental assisting).
notes: AMT's separate phlebotomy endowed scholarship accepts applications year-round.

name: Transportation YOU High School Scholarship
value: $2,500 (WTS International); chapter awards vary (e.g., WTS New Jersey $2,500, WTS Greater Chicago $2,000)
deadline: Set by each chapter; WTS International says its 2026 scholarships are closed and 2027 dates are not posted. Example: the WTS New Jersey 2026 deadline was September 18, 2026.
apply: Apply through your local WTS chapter's application (typically transcript, resume, recommendation letter and a personal statement of up to 500 words).
eligibility: Young women who are high school seniors studying STEM and planning a college degree in a transportation-related field; chapters may add requirements (e.g., WTS New Jersey requires a 3.0 weighted GPA).
notes: Chapter-based program; availability and dates depend on the local chapter.

name: Knights of Columbus Supreme Council Undergraduate Scholarships (Fourth Degree Pro Deo and Pro Patria, John W. McDevitt and endowed funds)
value: Up to $1,500 per year, renewable for up to four years of undergraduate study with satisfactory performance; number awarded depends on scholarship trust earnings
deadline: Page lists applications opening March 5 and closing April 22 (year not stated); 2027 dates not yet confirmed.
apply: Apply online through the ISTS portal (aim.applyISTS.net/KofC, program key KofC).
eligibility: Knights of Columbus members in good standing, children of members or of deceased members in good standing, or Columbian Squires, entering the freshman year as full-time bachelor's degree students at an approved Catholic college in the U.S. or its territories.
notes: Selection criteria for Pro Deo and Pro Patria and McDevitt awards are not stated on the page. The Percy J. Johnson and Frank L. Goularte endowed funds are need-based and require the FAFSA. Two Pro Deo and Pro Patria awards are reserved for Columbian Squires.

name: Scholarships for Military Children
value: 500 scholarships of $2,000 each for the 2027-2028 academic year
deadline: 2027-2028 application opens December 2026; closing date not yet posted.
apply: Student completes the online application personally: account, all form tabs, 500-word essay (topic announced at opening), transcript, and USID benefits number validation.
eligibility: Unmarried dependent children under 23 with a valid Uniformed Services ID card whose sponsor is active duty, Reserve/Guard, retired or deceased (Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, Coast Guard or Space Force), planning full-time enrollment in a bachelor's program or a transfer-track community college program. High school applicants need at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA.
notes: At least one recipient is chosen per commissary location with qualified applicants; remaining awards are allocated by applicant volume.

provider: Navy League of the United States
name: Navy League Foundation Scholarships
value: Named awards mostly $10,000 over four years; Frederick O. Harper $20,000 (4 years, engineering or bio sciences); Collins Aerospace $2,500 (1 year); Alaska Sea Service $1,000 per year (4 awards, Alaska residents)
deadline: 2027-2028 cycle opens October 15, 2026; closing date not yet posted.
apply: Online application with official transcript, FAFSA Student Aid Report, SAT/ACT scores, proof of military service and relationship, a recommendation letter and a brief biography.
eligibility: High school seniors entering an accredited college in the fall who are children, stepchildren, grandchildren or great-grandchildren of U.S. Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard or U.S.-flag Merchant Marine members, or who are themselves U.S. Naval Sea Cadet Corps cadets.
notes: Some named awards prefer STEM majors. The page does not say how merit and need are weighted, but a FAFSA SAR and test scores are required.

name: MCSF Undergraduate Scholarship
value: $2,500, $5,000, $7,500 or $10,000 per academic year; Children of the Fallen $30,000 over four years; Children of the Wounded up to $40,000 over four years
deadline: Undergraduate application window runs January 1 through March 1 each year.
apply: Apply online during the January 1 to March 1 window; decisions are emailed by May 31.
eligibility: Children or stepchildren of active duty, Reserve or veteran U.S. Marines (or Navy personnel attached to Marine units), with a minimum 2.00 GPA, family adjusted gross income of $134,000 or less for the 2025 tax year, and a high school diploma by August 1, 2027.
notes: Award amounts are based on financial need, GPA and available funding.

name: Purple Heart Foundation Academic Scholarship
value: Amount varies each year subject to funding levels
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was 5 p.m. on Monday, May 4, 2026.
apply: Submit the scholarship application package with essay and letters of recommendation.
eligibility: Purple Heart recipients and their spouses, children, stepchildren, adopted children, grandchildren or step-grandchildren who are accepted by or enrolled as full-time students (12 credit hours) at an accredited U.S. college, university or vocational school when the award is made. Graduate students are ineligible.
notes: Selection weighs academic achievement, extracurricular activities, community and military service, work experience, recommendations and essay. Not every applicant receives an award.

name: Dolphin Scholarships
value: $1,500 to $4,500 per year; maximum lifetime award $16,000 over 8 semesters; about 30 to 40 new scholarships each year
deadline: Applications reopen October 1, 2026; eligibility deadline February 15, 2027; full application deadline March 15, 2027.
apply: Complete eligibility screening by February 15, then the full application by March 15.
eligibility: Unmarried dependent children (under 24 at the March 15 deadline) or spouses of current or former qualified U.S. Navy Submarine Force members (6 years active duty in submarines or 8 years in submarine support), pursuing a first associate or bachelor's degree or vocational/technical certification.
notes: Scholars are selected on academic proficiency and commitment and excellence in school and community activities; financial need is considered after other aid is determined.

name: Anchor Scholarship Foundation Scholarships
value: Annual awards of $2,000 to $3,500; renewable options up to $10,000 over four years
deadline: Opens October 1; Step I closes March 1 and Step II closes April 1 at 11:59 PM EST (year not stated).
apply: Two-step online application (Step I, then Step II).
eligibility: High school seniors, college students or dependents pursuing a first full-time associate or bachelor's degree who are children or spouses of active duty, retired or honorably discharged Surface Navy personnel.
notes: Awarded on equal weighting of academic performance, character, extracurricular activities and financial need.

name: Daughters of the Cincinnati Military Star Scholarship
value: Up to $20,000 ($5,000 per year for four undergraduate years, subject to renewal requirements)
deadline: March 1 of the student's senior year of high school; the 2027 application cycle opens November 1, 2026.
apply: Submit the application, essay, secondary school report, community recommendation letter, Student Aid Report and proof of parent's military service.
eligibility: High school senior daughters of career commissioned officers in the U.S. Armed Forces planning full-time college enrollment.
notes: Awarded on academic merit combined with demonstrated financial need.

name: Sertoma Scholarship for Students Who Are Hard of Hearing or Deaf
value: Amount not stated on the official page
deadline: Application period runs November 1 to March 31 annually; awards apply to Fall 2027, Spring 2028 or Summer 2028.
apply: Apply online through the MyKaleidoscope portal linked from Sertoma's scholarship page.
eligibility: U.S. citizens with a minimum 40dB bilateral hearing loss (audiogram) who are high school seniors or undergraduates pursuing a full-time four-year bachelor's degree at a U.S. college, with a minimum 3.2 cumulative unweighted GPA.

name: Coast Guard Foundation Scholarships for Coast Guard Children
value: Annual awards of $2,500 or $5,000 paid to the school; students may reapply for up to four years
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; the 2026 season ran February 1 to April 1, 2026.
apply: Apply online through the Foundation's application portal during the spring window; a FAFSA report is required.
eligibility: High school seniors and college students who are dependents of active-duty Coast Guard members, reservists on active duty for at least 180 days, or retired Coast Guard members, attending college, trade school or technical programs.
notes: Review emphasizes academic achievement, leadership and community involvement; financial need factors into award levels.

name: Seabee Memorial Scholarship
value: Amount not stated on the official page
deadline: Applications accepted January 2 to April 15 each year (11:59 pm PDT); 2027 dates not separately posted.
apply: Online application with an official unweighted transcript (applications without an unweighted GPA are rejected).
eligibility: High school seniors who are children or grandchildren of active duty, reserve, retired or honorably discharged Seabees, pursuing accredited four-year, two-year or CTE programs.
notes: Selection is based on leadership, good citizenship, character, financial need and scholastic record.

name: FRA Education Foundation Scholarships
value: Up to $5,000; about $90,000 awarded each year
deadline: Applications accepted September 1 through April 15 each year (postmark); the 2026 form deadline was April 15, 2026 and the 2027 form is not yet posted.
apply: Mail the member or non-member application with essay, transcripts, recommendations and financial information, postmarked by April 15.
eligibility: U.S. citizens enrolling full time at an accredited trade school, community college or college who are FRA members or their spouses, children, grandchildren or great-grandchildren, or (non-member track) who have a personal or family connection to service in the U.S. Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard.
notes: Recipients are chosen on financial need, academic standing, character and leadership. FRA's separate Americanism Essay Contest is a different program.

name: Army Scholarship Foundation Scholarships
value: One-year scholarships awarded annually (amount not stated on the page)
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; applications are due April 15 of the application year.
apply: Online application with proof of service, transcript, IRS Form 1040, FAFSA summary, photo and an essay of up to 325 words on one of six topics.
eligibility: U.S. citizen high school seniors, graduates or undergraduates who are children of regular active duty, active duty Reserve or active duty National Guard U.S. Army members or of honorably discharged Army veterans (or spouses of enlisted soldiers), with a minimum 2.0 GPA, family AGI of $160,000 or less, under 24 (children of active members), and no prior bachelor's degree.
notes: Income cap applies.

name: Airmen Memorial Foundation Scholarship Program
value: $1,000 to $5,000 (including the $5,000 Major General Alfred K. Flowers Scholarship and several $2,000 to $2,500 named awards)
deadline: Application packages must be submitted no later than April 15 (2027 cycle not yet confirmed).
apply: Submit the application package online or by mail to HQAMF in Suitland, Maryland.
eligibility: Unmarried children, adopted children or stepchildren (age 23 or younger) of active duty, retired or veteran USAF, Air National Guard or Air Force Reserve members, who are high school seniors or full-time undergraduates accepted to an accredited college, have a GPA of 3.5 or higher, and depend on parents for over half of their support.
notes: Primarily academic; certain awards also consider disability, parent POW/MIA/KIA status, or extreme financial hardship. Scholarships are also promoted by the Air Force Sergeants Association.

provider: Jewish War Veterans of the USA Foundation
name: JWV National Youth Achievement Program Scholarships
value: Edith, Louis, and Max S. Millen Memorial Academic Award $2,000; Millen Memorial Athletic Award $2,000; Clifford Lee Kristal Education Award $1,250; Bernard Rotberg Memorial Award $1,000; Leon Brooks Memorial Award $1,000
deadline: Application period currently closed; 2027 deadline not yet posted. Recipients are chosen at the late-August National Convention and announced in September.
apply: Submit the JWV Foundation application when the period opens.
eligibility: High school seniors who are direct descendants of Jewish War Veterans members who joined prior to 2023.
notes: Detailed selection criteria are not posted on the official pages.

name: CPOSF Scholarships (including MCPON Scholarships)
value: Two $5,000 MCPON Scholarships plus about 20 to 50 $2,000 scholarships each year, depending on funds
deadline: Next cycle opens January 1, 2027; applications must be postmarked no later than April 1.
apply: Download the application and checklist and mail the packet to the fund in Newport, Rhode Island.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors, high school graduates or undergraduates who are dependent children, stepchildren or non-uniformed spouses of U.S. Navy Chief Petty Officers.
notes: Applications are scored by a panel of Chiefs and Senior Chiefs at the Senior Enlisted Academy using standard criteria; the merit/need balance is not published.

name: Tailhook Educational Foundation Scholarship
value: Over 100 scholarships a year, $3,500 to $20,000 per grant, averaging more than $5,000
deadline: Opens noon PT December 15, 2026; closes noon PT February 16, 2027.
apply: Online application on tailhook.net during the December to February window.
eligibility: High school graduates accepted for undergraduate enrollment at an accredited college who are children or grandchildren of current or former U.S. Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard Naval Aviators, Naval Flight Officers or Naval Aircrewmen, or of anyone who served aboard a U.S. Navy aircraft carrier.
notes: Awards are merit-based, except Gold Star students (who lost an active-duty parent-sponsor) are funded regardless of merit. Special enlisted scholarships and STEM emphasis.

name: Marine Corps League National Scholarship
value: Equal awards to all recipients; amount varies each year with the number of qualified applicants
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 application was due July 21, 2026 (proof of enrollment due September 21, 2026).
apply: Email the application and final transcript to Scholarship@MCLeague.org; selected applicants then submit a Student Data Sheet and proof of enrollment.
eligibility: Paid members of the Marine Corps League or its Auxiliary in good standing, or their spouses, children, stepchildren, grandchildren or great-grandchildren, and children of Marines or Navy FMF personnel killed in action, enrolled or accepted as full-time undergraduates (12+ credits) with a cumulative unweighted GPA of 3.30 or higher.
notes: Graduating seniors apply in summer after graduation and must include the official final high school transcript.

provider: Sons of Italy Foundation (Order Sons and Daughters of Italy in America)
name: Sons of Italy Foundation National Leadership Grants
value: $5,000 to $20,000 per scholarship; about 10 to 18 awarded annually depending on funding (per the 2026 cycle page)
deadline: Application opens October 5, 2026 and closes February 22, 2027 at 5:00 PM EDT
apply: Apply online through the SIF scholarship portal with essay, transcripts, and two letters of recommendation; the 2026 cycle charged a $35 non-refundable fee that included a one-year OSDIA membership.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors, undergraduates, and graduate/professional students who trace Italian ancestry to a parent or grandparent; U.S. citizens or green card holders; prior SIF recipients are ineligible.
notes: Merit-based (academic excellence and leadership). AI-generated essay content results in disqualification. Amount and fee figures come from the 2026 cycle page.

name: NIAF Scholarship Program
value: $2,500 to $12,000; nearly 200 scholarships administered annually
deadline: Application opens December 1, 2026; application and supporting documents due March 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. EST; decisions May 3, 2027
apply: Create an account on NIAF's CommunityForce portal and submit transcript, resume, recommendation letters, and FAFSA SAR.
eligibility: Students enrolling full-time at a U.S.-accredited institution for fall 2027 who hold an active NIAF membership (a parent, guardian, or grandparent's membership may be used) and demonstrate a commitment to or interest in Italian culture and heritage; U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
notes: Minimum 3.5 GPA generally; some named scholarships allow a lower GPA. FAFSA SAR is part of the application.

name: JACL National Scholarship Program (Entering Freshman Awards)
value: Nine named Entering Freshman awards within a program distributing over $70,000 annually; individual amounts not stated
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 freshman deadline was March 2, 2026, 11:59 p.m. HST.
apply: Submit the Freshman Application with personal statement, letter of recommendation, transcript, work experience, headshot, and JACL/community involvement records, plus proof of JACL membership.
eligibility: High school seniors planning full-time study at a U.S. college, university, or trade school who are active National JACL members (Individual or Student/Youth membership). JACL membership is open to people of any ethnic background.
notes: Applications for the 2026 cycle opened in December 2025. Some awards note preferences (field of study, financial aid eligibility).

name: NFB National Scholarship Program
value: Thirty $10,000 merit-based scholarships (more than $300,000 awarded annually)
deadline: 2027 application opens in December; the 2026 deadline was March 31, 2026.
apply: Complete the online application with required documents and proof of legal blindness, and complete an interview with the state NFB affiliate president.
eligibility: Legally blind students residing in the U.S., DC, or Puerto Rico pursuing full-time postsecondary degree study at a U.S. institution, including high school seniors entering college; finalists must attend the NFB National Convention in July.
notes: Awarded on academic excellence, community service, and leadership. The 2026 cycle required applicants to be at least 18 by the convention date.

name: ACB Scholarship Program
value: $2,000 to $7,500 per scholarship; 21 students received $112,300 in 2026
deadline: Applications for the 2027-2028 school year open November 1, 2026 and close February 14, 2027 at 11:59 pm CST
apply: Create an ACB account at members.acb.org and apply online with certification of legal blindness, transcripts, two recommendation letters, and proof of acceptance.
eligibility: Legally blind entering freshmen, undergraduates, graduate, and technical college students attending U.S. postsecondary institutions, full-time (or part-time while working 32+ hours weekly), with school and community involvement.
notes: A 3.0 GPA is required for most of the scholarships.

name: Lighthouse Guild Scholarship Program
value: Up to 20 undergraduate scholarships annually for high school seniors; unrestricted funds (amount not stated on the page)
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was February 28, 2026.
apply: Apply through the online Kaleidoscope portal with proof of legal blindness, proof of citizenship or legal residency, transcripts, three recommendation letters, and a personal statement of up to 500 words.
eligibility: Legally blind high school seniors going on to college (graduate students also eligible); U.S. citizens or legal residents.
notes: Merit-based, emphasizing academic excellence and community engagement.

name: Graeme Clark Scholarship
value: $2,000 per year for up to four consecutive years
deadline: Completed applications due online by September 30 of each year; applications typically open around March 31; winners notified by January 31
apply: Apply online through Cochlear's SmarterSelect portal; mailed applications are not accepted.
eligibility: Cochlear Nucleus implant recipients who are high school graduates or undergraduate/graduate students at accredited institutions; U.S. or Canadian citizens; minimum 3.0 unweighted GPA; at least 18 or with parental consent.
notes: Because applicants must be high school graduates, a fall 2027 entrant would typically apply in the cycle that closes September 30, 2027. Also open to Canadian citizens. Selection on academic achievement and commitment to leadership and humanity.

name: Anne Ford Scholarship
value: $10,000 ($2,500 per year over four years)
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was May 10, 2026 (rolling review).
apply: Submit the online application with disability documentation (IEP or psychologist letter), FAFSA/EFC information, at least one recommendation, and three personal essay responses (text, video, or audio).
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors with a documented learning disability (students with ADHD and a learning disability may apply) enrolling full-time in a four-year bachelor's program.
notes: Financial need factors into decisions; the committee looks for leadership potential for people with learning disabilities. The companion Allegra Ford Thomas Scholarship serves two-year and alternative paths.

name: Science Ambassador Scholarship
value: Five one-time $20,000 scholarships for the 2027 academic year
deadline: Monday, December 14, 2026 at 11:59 PM US Central Time
apply: Submit the application and a public three-minute YouTube video (16:9, not Shorts) teaching a STEM topic, with sources cited, at apply.scienceambassadorscholarship.org.
eligibility: Women and non-binary high school seniors or undergraduates pursuing a STEM major at a college in the U.S. or a U.S. territory; U.S. citizenship not required.
notes: Video must be a mini-lecture, not a personal statement. Finalists notified early 2027; winners announced spring 2027.

name: Point Foundation Flagship Scholarship
value: Up to $15,000 per year, up to four years of support, plus leadership development and mentoring
deadline: Application opens September 9 and closes November 19, 5:00 p.m. PST (for the fall 2027 term)
apply: Submit the Flagship application online.
eligibility: LGBTQ+ students and allies who are at least high school seniors, enrolling full-time in a bachelor's, graduate, or professional program at an accredited not-for-profit U.S. institution (not 100% online), with a minimum 3.3 cumulative GPA.
notes: Point uses a holistic evaluation that considers merit criteria as well as financial need.

provider: American Indian Science and Engineering Society (AISES)
name: Indigenous Peoples Education Fund Scholarship
deadline: Applications open December 15 and close April 30 annually
apply: Apply through the AISES scholarship application during the annual window.
eligibility: First-time freshmen enrolled full-time in a STEM field at an accredited college who are AISES members (free for students) and enrolled citizens or descendants of a tribe; minimum 3.0 GPA.
notes: Confirm with AISES whether high school seniors apply in spring before enrolling; the page says applicants must be a freshman (first-time student) enrolled full-time.

provider: AHEPA Educational Foundation (The Order of AHEPA)
name: AHEPA National Scholarships
value: Up to $2,500 for most programs; Chariclea Christodulakis-Cummins Scholarship $10,000 for a qualifying female high school graduate
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 applications were due March 31, 2026 by certified mail.
apply: Mail one package with the application, photo, official transcripts, two non-family recommendation letters, and financial documentation if applying for need-based awards.
eligibility: High school seniors, college, and graduate students of Hellenic descent or Philhellenes, where the applicant or an immediate family member is a paid member of AHEPA, Daughters of Penelope, Sons of Pericles, or Maids of Athena; minimum 3.0 GPA; family gross income under $100,000; U.S. citizens and permanent residents.
notes: Has both merit awards (scholastic achievement, SAT/ACT for seniors, honors, activities) and need-based awards; an income cap applies.

provider: National Society of High School Scholars (NSHSS)
name: NSHSS First Generation Scholarship
value: Amount not specified on the page
deadline: Application opens November 26, 2026; closing date not stated
apply: Submit a 500 to 800 word essay on first-generation challenges, academic resume, transcript, educator recommendation, headshot, and optional leadership media.
eligibility: NSHSS members who are first-generation college students: high school seniors and college freshmen, sophomores, and juniors.
notes: Merit-based, recognizing academic achievement and leadership. NSHSS membership required.

name: CBC Spouses Education Scholarship
value: Amount not stated on the program page
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; the 2026 application ran January 5 to March 27, 2026.
apply: Apply through the CBCF AcademicWorks portal (cbcfinc.academicworks.com).
eligibility: Academically talented and highly motivated African American or Black students pursuing undergraduate, graduate, or doctoral degrees.
notes: Detailed GPA, residency, and amount terms are not on the program page; contact scholarships@cbcfinc.org.

name: Stokes Educational Scholarship Program
value: Up to $30,000 per year for tuition and fees, plus year-round salary, summer internship housing/travel support and federal benefits
deadline: Applications open September 1 for the summer 2027 program; closing date not stated on the official page
apply: Apply through the NSA job board and email resume, transcript, SAT/ACT scores, two recommendation letters and the essay ("I want a career at NSA because...") to StokesHiring@uwe.nsa.gov.
eligibility: U.S. citizens who are high school seniors at the time of application, able to obtain a security clearance, with SAT 1200+ or ACT 25+ (3.0+ GPA preferred for STEM), majoring in artificial intelligence, computer science, computer/electrical engineering, cybersecurity, data science, mathematics or Chinese language analysis.
notes: Scholarship-for-service: graduates must work at NSA for at least 1.5 times the length of study.

name: Louis Stokes Education Scholarship (STOKES) Program
value: Tuition assistance (amount not stated), paid full-time summer work at DIA and guaranteed employment upon graduation
deadline: 2026-27 announcement not yet posted; announcements typically open in September or October
apply: High school guidance office reviews and submits the online application with transcript, SAT/ACT scores, DIA Form 418A, resume, essay on field of study and leadership, and FAFSA or tax return documentation.
eligibility: U.S. citizens (all immediate family members must also be citizens; dual citizens ineligible) who are high school seniors at the time of application, minimum 2.75 GPA, with demonstrated leadership, studying fields such as foreign area studies, computer science, business, public administration, international relations, political science, STEM, engineering or intelligence analysis.
notes: DIA describes STOKES as a needs-based program. Service commitment of up to 18 months per academic year sponsored.

name: CIA Undergraduate Scholarship Program
value: Up to $18,000 per academic year for tuition, mandatory fees and books (up to $25,000 for STEM majors), plus salary for summer work
deadline: CIA is currently not accepting applications for the Summer 2027 Stokes Scholar Program; next window not yet posted
apply: Apply through MyLINK with transcripts, proof of citizenship, tax forms and resume; high school seniors must provide college acceptance letters.
eligibility: U.S. citizens at least 18 at submission, including current high school seniors accepted to a four-year college, enrolled full time, with a minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale and household AGI up to $120,000 (dependents) or $50,000 (independent).
notes: Financial need (AGI ceiling) is required. Work obligation of 1.5 times the length of sponsorship, or repay tuition.

name: USDA 1890 National Scholars Program
value: Full tuition, fees, books, room and board, plus a USDA summer internship that may convert to full-time employment; renewable annually
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 application was available through March 8, 2026.
apply: Submit the online application through the USDA scholars portal with official transcripts and two 250 to 500 word essays.
eligibility: U.S. citizens entering or attending one of the 19 1890 land-grant universities, with a 3.0 GPA and at least 21 ACT or 1080 SAT, majoring in agriculture, food, natural resource sciences or related fields (e.g., agribusiness, animal science, forestry, nutrition, computer science).
notes: Restricted to 1890 land-grant universities.

name: Tuskegee Airmen Scholarship
value: $1,500 one-time first-year awards; 40 or more typically available each year
deadline: Set by each local Tuskegee Airmen, Inc. chapter; 2027 chapter deadlines not posted on the Foundation page
apply: Submit the completed application to the Tuskegee Airmen, Inc. chapter nearest your residence by that chapter's deadline (not to the Foundation).
eligibility: Students graduating from accredited high schools in the spring with at least a 3.0 GPA on a four-point scale, entering the first year of college, with interest in aviation, aerospace and science technology.
notes: Awards go to first-year students "who need help to pay for college"; parent tax documentation required.

name: Golden Apple Scholars of Illinois
value: Up to $23,000 in total support (tuition assistance and paid professional development)
deadline: Priority deadline December 1, 2026; final deadline March 1, 2027
apply: Online application with references, personal statements and unofficial transcript, followed by an interview. ACT/SAT optional except for homeschooled applicants.
eligibility: Illinois high school seniors (Class of 2027) who are U.S. citizens or eligible noncitizens and Illinois residents, planning to earn teacher licensure at a participating Illinois university.
notes: Must teach five years in an Illinois school-of-need within seven years of graduation; 2.5 GPA required to continue.

provider: CERRA (Center for Educator Recruitment, Retention, and Advancement)
name: South Carolina Teaching Fellows
value: Up to $24,000 ($6,000 per year for four years: up to $5,700 for tuition and expenses plus $300 for enrichment)
deadline: 2027 application dates not posted on the program page
apply: Apply through CERRA's Teaching Fellows application.
eligibility: South Carolina high school seniors with high academic achievement, a history of school and community service and/or work experience, who want to teach in South Carolina.
notes: Up to 230 Fellows a year, contingent on state funding. Fellows teach in a South Carolina public school one year for each year of funding.

name: DU National Scholarship Program
value: 61 awards: one $10,000 National Scholarship, ten $1,000 Conservation Scholarships and fifty $500 Varsity Scholarships
deadline: Application reopens October 15, 2026; 2027 deadline not yet posted
apply: Submit the online application with transcript, DU membership and volunteer history, awards list, up to three recommendation letters and an essay of up to 500 words on outdoor experiences and wetlands conservation.
eligibility: High school seniors who are Ducks Unlimited members with a cumulative GPA of 2.8 or higher; volunteer and conservation involvement weighted heavily.
notes: Awards usable at accredited community colleges, four-year colleges or trade/technical schools.

name: AGWT High School Senior Scholarships (Baroid, Stetson-Shahroody, Flexcon Industries)
value: $2,500 each (three scholarships; one award per student)
deadline: April 30 each year
apply: Complete the AGWT application form (one application may be considered for all three).
eligibility: High school seniors intending to pursue a career in a groundwater-related field.

name: GMiS STEM Scholarships
value: Merit awards $500 to $5,000; non-merit awards $500 to $1,000
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 application closed May 8, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST.
apply: Complete the online GMiS scholarship application and submit all documents by the deadline.
eligibility: Students enrolled in a STEM or health-related undergraduate or graduate program for the upcoming fall, including graduating high school seniors accepted to a four-year STEM degree program in the U.S. (varies by donor); merit awards require a 3.0 GPA. U.S. citizens, residents, F-1 and DACA students accepted.
notes: J-1 visa holders ineligible. Senior eligibility depends on each year's donor designations.
